N01.action: Establish MAIN, ENGINE, G1 and G2 and query both job layers.
N01.expect: MAIN in the unit job only; ENGINE, G1 and G2 in both jobs; exact creation times, parents, inner flags and token identity; children running, not merely created.

N02.action: MAIN closes its sole inner handle while it keeps running.
N02.expect: ENGINE, G1 and G2 signal without unit-job termination or an observer job duplicate; MAIN stays responsive and in the unit job until the final stop.

N03.action: Explicit stop with a cooperative ExecStop helper.
N03.expect: Helper runs once for the captured main; inner descendants, MAIN and helper exit; stop succeeds; no restart afterwards.

N04.action: Hung ExecStop helper and a MAIN that ignores the request, TimeoutStopSec=5s.
N04.expect: Forced cleanup removes both jobs' processes and the helper; stop reports failure within the budget; explicit stop stays down.

N05.action: Terminate the exact MAIN process under Restart=always.
N05.expect: Loss of the sole inner handle kills the engine tree; every old handle signals before the replacement launch; the new generation and invocation are contained.

N06.action: Crash the exact headless user-manager process with the unit enabled.
N06.expect: The old user manager, MAIN, ENGINE, G1 and G2 exit before the replacement MAIN is created; a new S4U manager restores the enabled workload.

N07.action: Crash the exact broker process; SCM recovery and enabled-unit restoration run through the installed daemon.
N07.expect: The old managed tree exits before the replacement MAIN is created; daemon and CLI bytes are unchanged; the new broker restores the enabled workload in a new generation.

N08.action: ENGINE, G1 and G2 commit 96 MiB each under MemoryMax=256M.
N08.expect: The unit-job commit limit is enforced and reported as a resource limit; the inner job has no limit to credit; the whole tree is cleaned up.

N09.action: Format 1 CPUQuota=25% with busy descendants, compared with an uncapped control.
N09.expect: Native CpuRate 2500 with a hard cap on the unit job, none on the inner job; measured use within the declared bound, or explicitly inconclusive.

N10.action: Format 2 WindowsCPUQuota=25%, same control and measurement.
N10.expect: Same native and measured scope as N09 using the format 2 directive.

N11.action: MAIN, ENGINE and G1 request CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB with no inner breakaway flags.
N11.expect: No created process is outside the unit job; every attempt and its result is recorded.

N12.action: After READY, set only inner BREAKAWAY_OK; ENGINE and G1 request breakaway for new probes.
N12.expect: Probes may leave the inner job but never the unit job; existing members keep inner membership; the unit stop removes every process.

N13.action: After READY, set only inner SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK; ENGINE and G1 create normal probes.
N13.expect: Probes stay in the unit job even when they leave the inner job; the unit stop removes every process.

N14.action: Kill MAIN at a held launch gate: pre-assign and pre-resume in assign mode, pre-resume in job-list mode.
N14.expect: The child's primary thread is still suspended; an unassigned child remains contained by the unit job, an assigned or atomically created child dies with the inner job; every child is drained before replacement.

N15.action: Sensitivity control: ENGINE deliberately inherits one inner-job duplicate; MAIN closes both of its copies, then ENGINE closes the last one.
N15.expect: The probe detects the inherited job; the tree survives MAIN's close and dies after ENGINE's. Not a safe production lane.

N16.action: A test-only seam fails the first cleanup of a real nested tree; request a start while it is held, then release and retry.
N16.expect: No replacement is launched or admitted while cleanup is unconfirmed; an early start return is a refusal; after release every held process exits, cleanup is confirmed and a fresh invocation succeeds.
